title: EU Platform Work Directive — Algorithmic management safeguards for platform workers
description: The algorithmic-management provisions of the EU's Platform Work Directive, regulating automated monitoring and decision-making systems used to manage platform/gig workers. Paraphrase pending verification against the primary EUR-Lex consolidated text — hence 'Community' confidence.
framework_name: Directive (EU) 2024/2831 on improving working conditions in platform work
control_text: Platforms using automated monitoring or decision-making systems affecting platform workers must: restrict processing of certain sensitive data categories (Art. 7); complete a data-protection impact assessment before deployment (Art. 8); inform workers and their representatives about the systems' use, purpose, and logic (Art. 9); provide human oversight and regular evaluation of the systems' impact on working conditions (Art. 10); and give workers the right to a human explanation of, and to contest, any significant automated decision — with certain decisions (including account restriction, suspension, or termination) prohibited from being taken by fully automated means without human review (Art. 11).

citations.title: Directive (EU) 2024/2831 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 23 October 2024 on improving working conditions in platform work

relationships.reason: Satisfying this control requires an observable record of worker disclosure and appeal.
